name: Ethiopia

findings.summary: Ethio Telecom launched pre-commercial 5G on six sites in Addis Ababa using Huawei and ZTE equipment, under temporary spectrum approval, planning up to 150 sites within a year.
findings.analyst_inference: Tier 2 because the launch was pre-commercial on a handful of sites. RCR names Huawei and ZTE; Mobile World Live names only Huawei. Current 5G vendor split across the national network is not established. Audit 2026-10-28: Scale -> municipal: pre-commercial launch on six sites in Addis Ababa (spec-required patch listed in AUDIT-2026-10-25).

findings.summary: Huawei was reported as main contractor for Ethio Telecom's latest 4G/LTE expansion, including the eastern part of the country; no site count or value given.
findings.analyst_inference: Coded tier 3 as a reported contract award; counterparty named but no value or award notice. OSIRIS item seen in search results only.

findings.summary: Huawei and ZTE shared a roughly US$1.6bn deal to build LTE in Addis Ababa and 3G nationwide for state monopoly Ethio Telecom, backed by low-interest vendor financing.
findings.analyst_inference: The opened page gives no year (it refers to Ethio Telecom as the only operator, so pre-2022); date left null rather than inferred. Pre-2020 in all likelihood, so still_current is null. Financier is described only as Chinese state-linked banks, so not named. Capacity headline (ZTE could lose the contract) seen in search only; a possible partial reversal not verified. Audit 2026-10-28: Telecoms.com (2013-08-19) confirms the US$1.6bn deal, US$800m each, with low-interest vendor financing; no state-linked banks named. Date set from it; corroborated with Fierce (independent S2).

findings.summary: At MWC 2026 Ethio Telecom signed a network expansion agreement with Ericsson covering about 1,500 sites: 4G capacity, new 5G, 75 off-grid rural sites and 3G-to-4G upgrades. Huawei and ZTE talks were reported concluded in principle only.
findings.analyst_inference: Single opened S3 source; no value disclosed. Ericsson is Swedish, so third. Signals Ethio Telecom adding a non-PRC RAN vendor alongside its Huawei/ZTE base, not replacing it; the Huawei/ZTE in-principle deals are not coded as findings since unsigned.

findings.summary: Safaricom Ethiopia reportedly picked Nokia for its core network and Addis Ababa coverage, as part of a planned US$8.5bn ten-year investment.
findings.analyst_inference: Capacity's report was labelled exclusive (unnamed sourcing). Capital Ethiopia headline (US$500m Nokia deal) seen in search only, so the value is not recorded. Nokia is Finnish, so third.

findings.summary: Safaricom Ethiopia reportedly picked Huawei to supply network coverage for the country outside Addis Ababa, with Nokia handling the core and the capital.
findings.analyst_inference: Single opened S2 source with unnamed sourcing; whether Huawei's role is RAN only is not stated. If accurate, Huawei RAN covers most of Safaricom Ethiopia's geography.

findings.summary: Raxio opened its ET1 data centre in Ethio ICT Park, Addis Ababa, with up to 3MW of IT load and 800 racks.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole us rests on DCD describing Raxio's parent Roha Group as a US-based investment firm; Raxio's own corporate domicile was not checked and other investors may hold stakes. Pole should be re-checked. Audit 2026-10-28: Connecting Africa (2023-11-22) confirms 3MW/800 racks but not the Roha Group parent or Ethio ICT Park; pole us still unverified (compare MOZ-004, pole null for Raxio).

findings.summary: Wingu.Africa broke ground on a data centre on a 15,000 sq m site at Ethio ICT Park, billed as Ethiopia's first hyperscale facility; capacity and value undisclosed.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole null: the source calls Wingu.Africa pan-African without stating its home jurisdiction or ownership. Tier 4 for construction started; operational status not confirmed in this pass. Audit 2026-10-28: DCD names Wingu.Africa as Djibouti-based, so the owner-operator home jurisdiction is Djibouti: pole null -> third. DCD also reports the facility has since been inaugurated (10MW, 800 racks at full build); inauguration date not recorded.

findings.summary: State-owned Ethio Telecom opened a Tier-III-ready modular data centre in Addis Ababa supplied by Huawei, holding up to 800 servers, for mobile money and business systems, with colocation and cloud planned.
findings.analyst_inference: Coded domestic as an owner-operated building with Huawei as builder. A prefabricated modular data centre is close to IT equipment (Huawei supplies power, cooling and management systems), so a reviewer could argue for prc; whether Huawei holds O&M access is not stated.

findings.summary: Ethio Telecom and Huawei signed a partnership to co-develop enterprise digital solutions spanning connectivity, cloud, AI, cybersecurity, IoT and data centres, including integration with Telebirr.
findings.analyst_inference: Coded tier 1 because the agreement's binding nature and value are undisclosed; it reads as a partnership framework. Layer applications chosen for enterprise solutions; cloud elements overlap the global cloud layer.

findings.summary: Addis Ababa's city administration entered a strategic partnership with Huawei to digitise public services and modernise urban-management technology; no value or contract terms published.
findings.analyst_inference: Republished Ecofin item; no surveillance or safe-city scope is stated, so this is not evidence of a Huawei safe-city system in Addis.

silicon.null_reason: no public accelerator purchases, GPU clusters or export-licence reporting for Ethiopia found in 1 targeted search; Addis Fortune mentions planned GPU clusters in Digital Ethiopia 2030 without vendor

models.null_reason: no government partnership with a frontier model provider or sovereign national model found in 1 search; the EAII tripartite MoU page (Fana, state-affiliated) was blocked; Addis AI is a private Amharic assistant with undisclosed base model

power.null_reason: power deals found are bitcoin-mining PPAs with EEP (e.g. Bitdeer 50MW Oromia, SEC 6-K May 2025) and EEP's Aug 2025 phase-out of crypto mining; none AI- or data-centre-specific

corrections.note: Source-verified corrections and audit notes: ETH-001, ETH-003, ETH-007, ETH-008

research_gaps: Current RAN/core vendor split for Ethio Telecom 4G/5G after the 2026 Ericsson agreement; did Huawei/ZTE in-principle deals at MWC26 get signed?
Confirm Safaricom Ethiopia vendors from primary sources (Safaricom IR/annual report) and whether Huawei supplies RAN only.
Year, value and financier of the US$1.6bn Huawei/ZTE Ethio Telecom deal, and whether ZTE's share was cut (Capacity headline).
Huawei or other safe-city/surveillance deployments for Addis Ababa police or INSA: no credible source found in this pass.
EAII tripartite MoU (Fana) parties and any foreign AI partners; EAII's 16,000 TB data centre vendor stack.
Raxio and Wingu.Africa corporate domicile and current operational status of Wingu's Addis campus.
Whether Ethio Telecom's Tele Cloud runs on a Huawei stack.
EEP crypto-mining phase-out (Aug 2025): any re-allocation of power to AI/data-centre loads.
